studies.label: Two-day classroom creative-writing experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 18 (printed SI p. 2), A.1, Participants; see also PDF p. 21 (printed SI p. 5), A.2 for story and evaluation counts
counts_source.quote: A total of 285 students successfully participated in the experiment.

arms.name: Human Confirmation
arms.description: Randomized AI-day mode: AI handles ideation, outlining, drafting, and editing. Students prompt, accept or reject output, or request regeneration, and may not introduce their own ideas (PDF p. 18, printed SI p. 2, A.1).

arms.name: Human Creativity
arms.description: Randomized AI-day mode: students ideate and outline without AI, then ChatGPT drafts and edits; students prompt and accept or reject during production without adding ideas or directly writing/editing (PDF pp. 18-19, printed SI pp. 2-3, A.1).

arms.name: Copilot
arms.description: Randomized AI-day mode: humans and ChatGPT collaborate iteratively throughout all stages; either may initiate and the student may contribute, refine, or request suggestions. Unrestricted comparator for Atlas coding; the paper's regression reference is Human Confirmation (PDF p. 19, printed SI p. 3, A.1).

arms.name: Writing without AI (Day 1)
arms.description: Shared fixed-order baseline: everyone first writes manually without AI. This is not a separately randomized no-AI arm or an after-AI outcome (PDF p. 4).

studies.task: Students in an elective emerging-technologies course wrote a new 1,000-word short story in any genre on each study day, without AI first and using the assigned AI collaboration mode second (PDF p. 4; PDF pp. 18-19, printed SI pp. 2-3).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT 3.5
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Experimental Design; PDF p. 8, Discussion and Limitations. Model release year is not printed.

studies.shared_sample: No participant overlap with another paper is stated in the screening form or paper. The ancillary S2 autonomous-model DAT comparison reuses this cohort's baseline DAT scores and is not a separate human sample (PDF p. 8).

estimates.notes: The analysis is between individually randomized AI modes on the AI writing day; within_person is null. The paper gives no contrast-specific people or rating counts. Arm means and their intervals are plotted in Figure 2 without text values usable under the extraction rule, so they are null. Table 1's pooled descriptive statistics cover all modes and both days and are not arm statistics. Repeated ratings of a writer are not accounted for in the stated regression specification; no clustering or participant random effect is reported (PDF p. 23, printed SI p. 7, A.3). No participant-level SD or standardized effect is printed. Printed precision is retained in source quotes. This pair is reported only as showing no significant difference; no coefficient is calculated by subtracting the other mode coefficients.

open_items: Exact randomized and analyzed people by arm and outcome are unreported. The participating-cohort total is not explicitly a randomized or deduplicated analyzed total. Story, survey, and rating counts cannot substitute for people counts (PDF pp. 11, 18, 21).

The rating outcomes lack printed arm-specific means, SDs, and participant-level uncertainty. Table 1 aggregates all AI modes and the no-AI baseline; Tables S4/S7 do not supply regression sample sizes or the SE estimator.

The rating-level models do not state whether repeated evaluations of each writer/story or shared evaluators are accommodated (PDF p. 23, printed SI p. 7; PDF pp. 48 and 51, printed SI pp. 32 and 35). These printed SEs cannot be treated as participant-level precision.

The interval and significance-test methods for semantic similarity, genre similarity, and genre counts are not stated. Similarity scores depend on the other stories in the same condition; treatment of that dependence is not explained (PDF pp. 6-7, 16).

The schema has one CI slot. For the similarity and genre-count records it stores the treatment mean's CI, while the control mean's printed CI is retained verbatim in notes and its source quote. No difference CI or SE is derived.

Some published regression coefficients are control minus treatment under the required arm orientation. Their printed signs are retained and their direction is explicit in difference_is, regression.model, and notes; downstream use must respect that direction.
No exact overall-quality coefficient, SE, or p-value is printed for Human Creativity versus Copilot. The comparison is retained with null statistics and the paper's qualitative finding (PDF p. 5).
The extraction vocabulary has no exact measure code for cosine similarity of binary genre vectors. S1-O7 therefore retains measure=null, with the confirmed method in measure_detail (PDF p. 16).
Recruitment and the main text specify 105-minute writing sessions, while the SI task descriptions specify 75 minutes; the discrepancy remains unresolved (PDF pp. 4, 18-19).
The study country and ChatGPT 3.5 release year are not explicitly reported; no values are inferred from author affiliations, model-name knowledge, or the manuscript filename.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-11. The entire markdown conversion was read in successive chunks through the SI references; the detailed methods were also read before continuing the results. Every cited PDF page was checked using PyMuPDF text extraction, with find_tables used for Tables S4/S7. Only the randomized AI-mode comparisons enter estimates. There is no randomized AI-versus-no-AI comparison and no unassisted post-AI assessment. The paper reports 285 participating students (PDF p. 18), 280 initial-survey records (PDF p. 11), and 549 stories, comprising 278 baseline and 271 AI-day stories, with 2,196 evaluations (PDF p. 21); these different units are not relabeled as analysis-specific people counts. The exact manuscript version is resolved by the supplied citation record and the matching local PDF hash. S2 is excluded, not counted as an additional eligible study. The qualitative genre-composition records preserve S1-O9 without transcribing numbers obtainable only from Figure 4A. Adjusted and unadjusted overall-quality models are separate records; rounded main-text differences accompany the adjusted records and are not extra estimates. No statistical quantities, p-values, effect sizes, counts, or interval endpoints were computed.
